# Imbalance handling comparison (generated by `experiments/imbalance_comparison.py`)

Rows 1-4: identical hotel split, TF-IDF fitted on training hotels only, C = 4.0; only the balancing method varies.
Rows 5-6: random row split, to show what applying SMOTE *before* splitting does to the reported numbers.

| Method | Test negative rate | PR-AUC | ROC-AUC | Precision at 80% recall | Recall @ 0.5 | Precision @ 0.5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| no balancing (current model) | 0.065 | 0.849 | 0.975 | 0.745 | 0.713 | 0.844 |
| class_weight='balanced' | 0.065 | 0.835 | 0.974 | 0.711 | 0.876 | 0.564 |
| random oversampling (train only) | 0.065 | 0.829 | 0.973 | 0.687 | 0.861 | 0.584 |
| SMOTE (train only) | 0.065 | 0.818 | 0.972 | 0.673 | 0.852 | 0.584 |
| LEAKY: SMOTE before split (random split) | 0.500 | 0.992 | 0.993 | 0.988 | 0.983 | 0.955 |
| reference: same random split, no SMOTE | 0.084 | 0.863 | 0.974 | 0.766 | 0.688 | 0.868 |
